subject.title: feat(linux): Quick Chat agent switcher, avatars, per-agent routing, and configurable shortcut

question: May Linux Quick Chat load arbitrary `http:` and `https:` identity-avatar URLs from the local desktop webview?
rationale: The current behavior deliberately broadens a webview network boundary; choosing between avatar parity and a local-only image policy is a product/security decision that tests cannot resolve.

options.title: Keep Quick Chat avatars local-only
options.body: Preserve the current `self`/`data:` image CSP and omit remote avatar URLs from Quick Chat rendering while retaining emoji and monogram fallbacks.

options.title: Accept remote avatar fetching
options.body: Allow remote identity-avatar URLs and document the intentional outbound image-request and network-boundary behavior for Linux desktop users.

options.title: Design a constrained remote-avatar path
options.body: Pause this portion until maintainers choose a validated or proxied image-loading model with an explicit host, protocol, and privacy policy.

recommendation.title: Keep Quick Chat avatars local-only
recommendation.body: Preserve the current `self`/`data:` image CSP and omit remote avatar URLs from Quick Chat rendering while retaining emoji and monogram fallbacks.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature lineage and current implementation both trace to this author, including the earlier merged Linux Quick Chat foundation.
